examples.en: I want to get into university by my own efforts.
It's hard to solve this on my own.

examples.ko: 이번 시즌 자력 우승은 이미 어려워졌어요.
examples.en: Winning the title on their own results is already out of reach this season.
I got a home entirely on my own, without any help.
The will to stand on your own feet to the end is important.
My own efforts alone weren't enough, so I asked a friend for help.

explain: '혼자 힘으로'와 같은 뜻이지만 더 딱딱해서 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요. 보통 '자력으로' 꼴로 쓰고, 짝말은 남의 힘을 뜻하는 '타력'이에요. 자석의 힘을 뜻하는 '자력'(磁力)도 소리가 같아서 문맥으로 구분해야 해요.
explain_en: It means the same as '혼자 힘으로' (by oneself) but sounds more formal, so you see it in writing and news. It is usually used as '자력으로', and its counterpart is '타력' (others' power). There is also a same-sounding '자력' (磁力, magnetic force), so you tell them apart by context.

examples.ko: 아기 이름 작명은 할머니께서 해 주셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother chose the baby's name for us.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 작명 센스가 정말 좋아요.
examples.en: This shop has a really great sense for naming things.
Naming is hard, so I've been agonizing over it for days.
We got the baby's name from a naming house.
We picked the puppy's name from a naming contest.

examples.ko: 게임 캐릭터 작명에 두 시간이나 걸렸어요.
examples.en: Naming my game character took a whole two hours.

explain: 사람 이름뿐 아니라 가게, 제품, 반려동물 이름을 지을 때도 써요. 일상에서는 '이름 짓기'라고도 하고, '작명 센스'는 이름을 재치 있게 잘 지었을 때 칭찬하는 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used not only for people's names but also for shops, products and pets. In everyday talk you can also say '이름 짓기'. '작명 센스' is a common way to praise someone for coming up with a clever name.

examples.en: How did you come up with the name for your new cafe?
I named my new puppy 'Tofu'.

examples.ko: 새 가게를 멋지게 작명해 줄 사람을 찾아요.
examples.en: I'm looking for someone to give my new shop a great name.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 별명을 재미있게 작명해 줬어요.
examples.en: My friend gave me a funny nickname.

examples.ko: 작명하기 전에 이름의 뜻을 꼭 확인하세요.
examples.en: Be sure to check the meaning of a name before you choose it.

examples.ko: 신제품을 작명하느라 회의를 세 번이나 했어요.
examples.en: We had three meetings just to name the new product.

explain: 일상에서는 '이름을 짓다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요. '작명하다'는 조금 딱딱하거나, 가게·제품·별명처럼 이름을 붙이는 일을 말할 때 써요.
explain_en: In daily life '이름을 짓다' sounds much more natural. '작명하다' is a bit formal and is used for giving names to shops, products or nicknames.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 들어온 타이밍이 정말 절묘했어요.
examples.en: The timing of his entrance was truly perfect.
A beautifully timed goal went in late in the match.

examples.ko: 이 책은 제목을 정말 절묘하게 지었네요.
examples.en: This book's title is really cleverly chosen.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 만난 시기가 너무 절묘해서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was amazed at how perfectly timed it was that the two met.
The twist in this movie is really masterful.
'Exquisite' is exactly the right word for this painting.

explain: '교묘하다'는 속임수처럼 나쁜 쪽에도 쓰지만 '절묘하다'는 대체로 칭찬이에요. 타이밍, 비유, 위치, 표현처럼 딱 들어맞아서 감탄할 때 써요.
explain_en: '교묘하다' can also describe sly, bad things like tricks, but '절묘하다' is mostly praise. Use it for timing, metaphors, placement or wording that fits so perfectly it makes you admire it.

examples.en: The government announced a plan to increase rice production.

examples.ko: 겨울이 오기 전에 석유 증산이 필요하다는 뉴스를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw news saying oil production needs to rise before winter.

examples.ko: 공장은 증산을 위해 직원을 더 뽑고 있어요.
examples.en: The factory is hiring more workers to boost production.

examples.ko: 증산 결정 이후 가격이 조금 내려갔어요.
examples.en: Prices dropped a little after the decision to raise production.

examples.ko: 이 회사는 올해 반도체 증산에 힘을 쏟고 있어요.
examples.en: This company is putting great effort into producing more chips this year.

examples.ko: 농민들은 증산보다 품질이 더 중요하다고 말해요.
examples.en: Farmers say quality matters more than higher output.

explain: 반대말은 '감산'이에요. 쌀, 석유, 반도체처럼 만들어 내는 물건의 양을 늘린다는 뉴스에서 주로 나와요. 일상에서는 '더 많이 만들다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '감산' (production cut). It mostly appears in news about raising the output of goods such as rice, oil or chips. In daily talk people say '더 많이 만들다'.

examples.en: The company will produce more of the product starting next month.
They decided not to increase rice production this year.
Demand rose, so the factory quickly ramped up production.
To raise output, we have to bring in more machines.
If oil-producing countries pump more oil, fuel prices go down.

examples.ko: 그 농장은 딸기를 증산해서 해외에도 팔아요.
examples.en: That farm grew more strawberries and sells them overseas too.

explain: '쌀을 증산하다'처럼 늘리는 물건이 목적어로 와요. 반대말은 '감산하다'예요. 일상에서는 '더 많이 만들다'라고 해요.
explain_en: The thing being increased comes as the object, as in '쌀을 증산하다'. The opposite is '감산하다'. In daily talk people say '더 많이 만들다'.

examples.ko: 특허 출원 서류를 다음 주에 내요.
examples.en: I'm submitting the patent application documents next week.

examples.ko: 상표 출원을 하려면 비용이 얼마나 들어요?
examples.en: How much does it cost to file a trademark application?

examples.ko: 출원 결과는 몇 달 뒤에 나와요.
examples.en: The result of the application comes out in a few months.

examples.ko: 출원이 늦어져서 다른 회사가 먼저 등록했어요.
examples.en: Our filing was late, so another company registered it first.
This design is already being applied for.

examples.ko: 출원 전에 아이디어를 공개하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't make your idea public before filing.

explain: 특허, 상표, 디자인 같은 권리를 정식으로 신청할 때 써요. '특허 출원', '상표 출원'처럼 정해진 말과 같이 나오는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is used when formally applying for rights such as a patent, trademark or design. It often appears in set pairings like '특허 출원' and '상표 출원'.

en: apply for; file an application for

examples.en: We filed the new technology as a patent.
I'm going to file the company name as a trademark.
It's safer to file this idea first.
I heard he filed applications for as many as three inventions.
Sir, when did you file for that design?
After you file, you have to wait for the examination.

explain: '특허를 출원하다', '상표를 출원하다'처럼 권리를 신청할 때 써요. 입학이나 취업은 '출원'이 아니라 '지원하다'를 써요.
explain_en: It is used for applying for rights, as in '특허를 출원하다' and '상표를 출원하다'. For admissions or jobs, use '지원하다' instead, not '출원하다'.

examples.ko: 동생이 태어나자 아이가 퇴행 행동을 보였어요.
examples.en: When the little brother was born, the child showed regressive behavior.
Joint degeneration begins as we get older.

examples.ko: 퇴행 현상은 스트레스 때문에 생기기도 해요.
examples.en: Regression can also be caused by stress.
I'm worried about the regression of talking like a baby again.
I go to the hospital because of degenerative arthritis.
Many people worry about the backsliding of democracy.

explain: 심리에서는 아이가 어린 시절의 행동으로 돌아가는 것, 의학에서는 '퇴행성 관절염'처럼 몸의 기능이 나빠지는 것을 말해요. '퇴보'와 비슷하지만 퇴행은 심리·의학 말로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: In psychology it means a child going back to earlier behavior, and in medicine it means the body's function declining, as in '퇴행성 관절염'. It is close to '퇴보' (regress), but '퇴행' shows up often in psychology and medicine.

examples.en: When a younger sibling arrives, the oldest child sometimes regresses.

examples.ko: 아이가 갑자기 아기처럼 말해서 퇴행한 것 같아요.
examples.en: The child suddenly talked like a baby, so it seems he regressed.

examples.ko: 몸의 기능이 퇴행하지 않게 운동을 해요.
examples.en: I exercise so that my body's functions don't decline.
Even adults regress when they are under heavy stress.

examples.ko: 사회가 퇴행한다는 말이 나올 만큼 상황이 안 좋아요.
examples.en: Things are so bad that people say society is moving backward.

examples.ko: 아이가 퇴행하는 모습을 보여도 혼내지 마세요.
examples.en: Even if the child shows signs of regression, don't scold him.

explain: '아이가 퇴행하다', '사회가 퇴행하다'처럼 주어가 스스로 뒤로 가는 느낌이라 목적어를 받지 않아요. 반대말은 '발전하다', '성장하다'예요.
explain_en: It describes the subject itself moving backward, as in '아이가 퇴행하다' or '사회가 퇴행하다', so it takes no object. Opposites are '발전하다' and '성장하다'.

examples.ko: 경찰의 회유에도 그는 입을 열지 않았어요.
examples.en: Even with the police coaxing him, he didn't open his mouth.
You shouldn't fall for sweet-talking persuasion.

examples.ko: 회유와 협박을 번갈아 쓰는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people alternate between coaxing and threatening.
His attempt to win people over didn't work.

examples.ko: 부모님의 회유 끝에 결국 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: After much coaxing from my parents, I finally went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 회유가 안 통하자 그는 화를 냈어요.
examples.en: When coaxing didn't work, he got angry.

explain: '달래다'는 따뜻한 느낌이지만 '회유'는 좋은 조건이나 말로 상대를 내 쪽으로 돌려놓으려는 의도가 있어요. 그래서 '회유와 협박'처럼 다소 부정적인 문맥에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: '달래다' feels warm, but '회유' carries an intention to bring someone over to your side with good terms or words. So it often appears in somewhat negative contexts like '회유와 협박' (coaxing and threats).

examples.en: I talked my friend around and brought him onto the same team.
The boss tried to win over the employee who wanted to leave with money.

examples.ko: 아무리 회유해도 그 사람은 마음을 안 바꿔요.
examples.en: No matter how much you coax him, he won't change his mind.
I bought the child a snack to coax him.
It seems the other side is trying to win us over.
Coaxing or threatening people is not right.

explain: '사람을 회유하다'처럼 목적어는 사람이에요. '설득하다'는 중립적이지만 '회유하다'는 이익이나 달콤한 말로 꾀어 내 편으로 만들려는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: The object is a person, as in '사람을 회유하다'. '설득하다' is neutral, but '회유하다' suggests luring someone to your side with benefits or sweet words.

examples.en: I went to the hospital for a chest X-ray.
My chest felt tight and breathing was hard, so I got tested.

examples.ko: 축구를 하다가 공에 맞아 흉부를 다쳤어요.
examples.en: I was hit by the ball playing soccer and hurt my chest.

examples.ko: 흉부 통증이 계속되면 바로 병원에 가세요.
examples.en: If the chest pain continues, go to the hospital right away.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 청진기로 흉부 소리를 들어 봤어요.
examples.en: The doctor listened to my chest sounds with a stethoscope.

examples.ko: 흉부 수술을 받은 뒤에 회복 중이에요.
examples.en: I'm recovering after chest surgery.

explain: 일상에서는 '가슴'이라고 하고, '흉부'는 병원이나 진단서에서 몸 부위를 말할 때 써요. 배 쪽은 '복부'예요. '가슴'은 마음이라는 뜻으로도 쓰지만 '흉부'는 몸 부위만 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily life people say '가슴'; '흉부' is used in hospitals and medical documents for this body part. The belly area is '복부'. '가슴' can also mean 'heart/feelings', but '흉부' only refers to the body part.

examples.en: He is going through the parole review.

examples.ko: 가석방 조건을 어기면 다시 감옥에 가야 해요.
examples.en: If you break the parole conditions, you have to go back to prison.
News came out that parole had been decided.

examples.ko: 가석방 기간에는 정해진 규칙을 지켜야 해요.
examples.en: During the parole period, you must follow the set rules.

examples.ko: 이번에 가석방 대상이 된 사람은 몇 명이에요?
examples.en: How many people are eligible for parole this time?

examples.ko: 가석방으로 나온 뒤 새 일자리를 구했어요.
examples.en: After getting out on parole, he found a new job.

explain: '석방'은 풀려난다는 말이고, '가석방'은 형기를 다 채우기 전에 조건을 지키는 전제로 나오는 거라 규칙을 어기면 다시 들어가요. 형이 끝나서 나오는 '만기 출소'와 달라요. 주로 뉴스나 법 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: '석방' just means being released, while '가석방' means getting out before the sentence ends on the condition of following rules, and breaking them can send you back. It differs from '만기 출소' (release at the end of the term). It appears mostly in news and legal talk.

examples.en: The Ministry of Justice paroled some well-behaved prisoners.
If they pass the review, they can be paroled.
The corrections authorities decided to parole him.
They parole people with good conduct first.

examples.ko: 너무 일찍 가석방하면 안 된다는 의견도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people think they shouldn't parole prisoners too early.

examples.ko: 어제 가석방한 사람이 모두 몇 명이에요?
examples.en: How many people in total were paroled yesterday?

explain: 주어는 법무부나 교도소 같은 기관이고, 목적어는 수감자예요. 풀려나는 사람 입장에서는 '가석방으로 나오다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: The subject is an institution such as the Ministry of Justice or a prison, and the object is the prisoner. From the released person's side, people say things like '가석방으로 나오다'.

examples.en: I went to the hospital for a thyroid test.
I'm worried because they said there's a lump on my thyroid.
When thyroid hormone is low, you get tired easily.
My mother takes thyroid medicine every day.

examples.ko: 목 앞쪽에 있는 갑상선이 부어서 아팠어요.
examples.en: The thyroid at the front of my neck was swollen and hurt.

examples.ko: 갑상선 수술은 잘 끝났고 지금은 회복 중이에요.
examples.en: The thyroid surgery went well and I'm recovering now.

explain: 일상 대화에서도 다른 쉬운 말 없이 그대로 '갑상선'이라고 해요. 병원에서는 '갑상선 기능 저하증', '갑상선 기능 항진증'처럼 병 이름에 붙어서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: There is no easier everyday word, so people say '갑상선' even in casual conversation. At the hospital it often appears in disease names such as '갑상선 기능 저하증' (hypothyroidism) and '갑상선 기능 항진증' (hyperthyroidism).

examples.ko: 두 나라의 갈등이 점점 격화되고 있어요.
examples.en: The conflict between the two countries is gradually intensifying.

examples.ko: 요즘 가전 시장에서 가격 경쟁이 크게 격화됐어요.
examples.en: Price competition has intensified greatly in the home appliance market lately.
I left the spot before the argument escalated.
The fiercer the competition gets, the better the service becomes.

examples.ko: 논쟁이 너무 격화돼서 아무도 말을 못 했어요.
examples.en: The debate got so heated that no one could speak.
The teacher stepped in so the fight wouldn't escalate.

explain: 갈등, 경쟁, 논쟁, 싸움처럼 맞서는 일이 더 거세질 때 써요. '심해지다'보다 딱딱한 말이고, 반대 느낌은 '완화되다', '누그러지다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when something adversarial like a conflict, competition, debate or fight becomes fiercer. It is more formal than '심해지다', and the opposite feelings are '완화되다' and '누그러지다'.

examples.en: As the conflict intensified, communication broke off.
As the negotiations dragged on, the opposition escalated.

examples.ko: 경쟁이 격화하는 시장에서 살아남기 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It isn't easy to survive in a market where competition is intensifying.

examples.ko: 논쟁이 격화하지 않게 서로 한 걸음씩 물러섰어요.
examples.en: Each side stepped back so the debate wouldn't escalate.
I didn't know the conflict would escalate this much.
Even as the criticism intensified, he answered calmly.

explain: 뜻과 주어(갈등·경쟁·대립)는 '격화되다'와 거의 같고, 목적어 없이 스스로 거세지는 느낌이에요. 무언가를 일부러 더 거세게 만든다고 할 때는 '격화시키다'를 써요.
explain_en: The meaning and typical subjects (conflict, competition, opposition) are almost the same as '격화되다', and it takes no object, with things growing fiercer on their own. To say someone deliberately makes something fiercer, use '격화시키다'.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 돈 문제와 결부돼 있어요.
examples.en: This problem is tied to money matters.
Might the two incidents be connected?
Health is deeply linked to lifestyle habits.
Happiness isn't tied only to success.
When it's linked to grades, students get more nervous.

examples.ko: 이 정책은 환경 문제와 결부돼서 논란이 커졌어요.
examples.en: This policy got linked with environmental issues and the controversy grew.

explain: 'A는 B와 결부되다'처럼 '와/과'를 써요. '연결되다'가 실제로 이어지는 느낌이라면 '결부되다'는 서로 관계가 있다고 묶여 보이는 느낌이에요. '관련되다', '연관되다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: It takes '와/과', as in 'A는 B와 결부되다'. While '연결되다' feels like things are actually joined, '결부되다' feels like two things are seen as bound together by a relationship. It is close to '관련되다' and '연관되다'.

examples.en: Please don't think of the two matters as linked.
Why do you tie every problem to age?

examples.ko: 그는 성공을 운과 결부시키는 걸 싫어해요.
examples.en: He dislikes attributing success to luck.

examples.ko: 그 일을 제 실수와 결부시킬 필요는 없어요.
examples.en: There's no need to link that matter to my mistake.

examples.ko: 성적을 용돈과 결부시켰더니 아이가 열심히 공부했어요.
examples.en: After I tied grades to allowance, the child studied hard.
If you force a link between the incidents, misunderstandings arise.

explain: 'A를 B와 결부시키다'처럼 말하는 사람이 둘을 엮어서 본다는 뜻이에요. '결부시키지 마세요'나 '억지로 결부시키다'처럼 쓰면 무리하게 엮는다는 느낌이 있어요. 스스로 연결되어 있는 경우는 '결부되다'를 써요.
explain_en: It means the speaker ties two things together, as in 'A를 B와 결부시키다'. In phrases like '결부시키지 마세요' or '억지로 결부시키다' it carries a sense of forcing a link. When the link exists on its own, use '결부되다'.

examples.ko: 아이의 숨은 재능을 계발해 주는 프로그램이에요.
examples.en: It's a program that helps bring out a child's hidden talents.
I draw every day to develop my creativity.
More people are developing their abilities on their own.
I developed my talent through a hobby.

examples.ko: 잠재력을 계발하면 더 큰 일을 할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you develop your potential, you can do bigger things.
It's a pity if you can't develop your potential.

explain: '개발하다'와 소리가 비슷하지만, '계발하다'는 재능, 능력, 창의력처럼 사람 안에 있는 가능성을 키울 때 써요. 상품, 기술, 땅은 '개발하다'를 써요. '자기계발'이라는 말로 많이 만나요.
explain_en: It sounds close to '개발하다', but '계발하다' is for nurturing the potential inside a person, such as talent, ability or creativity. For products, technology or land, use '개발하다'. You'll often meet it in the word '자기계발' (self-development).

examples.ko: 무직자는 대출 심사가 더 까다로울 수 있어요.
examples.en: Loan screening can be stricter for people without a job.

examples.ko: 저는 지금 무직자지만 곧 취직할 거예요.
examples.en: I'm unemployed right now, but I'll get a job soon.

examples.ko: 무직자도 청년 지원금을 신청할 수 있대요.
examples.en: I heard even people without jobs can apply for the youth support fund.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 무직자라서 카드를 만들기 어려웠어요.
examples.en: He had no job, so it was hard for him to get a card.
I gathered job information that unemployed people need.

examples.ko: 무직자 비율이 조금 줄었다는 기사가 나왔어요.
examples.en: An article came out saying the share of people without jobs fell slightly.

explain: 서류나 통계에서 '직업: 무직'처럼 쓰는 딱딱한 말이라, 사람에게 직접 쓰면 차갑게 들릴 수 있어요. 일자리를 찾는 사람은 '구직자'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a stiff word from forms and statistics, as in '직업: 무직', so using it directly about a person can sound cold. A person looking for work is called a '구직자' (job seeker).

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 이번 시즌 무패 행진을 이어 가고 있어요.
examples.en: Our team is continuing its unbeaten streak this season.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 데뷔 이후 무패로 은퇴했어요.
examples.en: That player retired undefeated since his debut.
Ten games unbeaten is really impressive.

examples.ko: 그 팀의 무패 기록이 드디어 깨졌어요.
examples.en: That team's unbeaten record has finally been broken.
We're training with the goal of winning the title unbeaten.
The team that boasted of being unbeaten lost for the first time.

explain: '지지 않았다'는 뜻이라 비긴 경기가 있어도 무패예요. 모두 이긴 '전승'과 달라요. 반대말은 '전패'예요. 스포츠에서 주로 써요.
explain_en: It means 'never lost', so a record with draws is still '무패'. That differs from '전승', which means winning every game. The opposite is '전패'. It is mainly used in sports.

examples.en: When spring came, the seeds began to germinate.
Germinated brown rice is softer than regular brown rice.
I chose seeds with a high germination rate.
This seed takes about a week to sprout.
The seed of the new business was a small conversation.
Bean sprouts are grown by using the germination of beans.

explain: 일상에서는 '싹이 트다', '싹이 나다'라고 말하고, '발아'는 과학이나 농업 이야기에서 많이 써요. 새로운 생각이나 움직임이 처음 생기는 것을 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: In daily talk people say '싹이 트다' or '싹이 나다', while '발아' is common in science and farming. It can also be used figuratively for a new idea or movement first appearing.

examples.en: The seeds sprouted in just a week.
If you give enough water, they sprout.
Do these beans sprout even in dark places?

examples.ko: 씨앗이 발아하려면 적당한 온도와 물이 필요해요.
examples.en: For seeds to sprout, they need suitable temperature and water.

examples.ko: 아직 발아하지 않은 씨앗은 따로 두세요.
examples.en: Set aside the seeds that haven't sprouted yet.

examples.ko: 작은 관심에서 발아한 아이디어가 큰 사업이 됐어요.
examples.en: An idea that sprouted from a small interest became a big business.

explain: 주어는 씨앗이나 콩 같은 식물이고 목적어는 받지 않아요. 일상에서는 '싹이 트다'라고 해요. 비유로 아이디어나 생각이 처음 생길 때도 써요.
explain_en: The subject is a plant part such as a seed or bean, and it takes no object. In daily talk people say '싹이 트다'. It can also be used figuratively when an idea first takes shape.
